newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GIDDINS LOSES APPEAL OVER DRUGS BAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GIDDINS LOSES APPEAL OVER DRUGS BAN.

text.p: Former Sussex bowler Ed Giddins on Friday lost his appeal against his 19-month ban for failing a drugs test.

The England A seamer, banned by the Test and County Cricket Board's disciplinary committee in August after testing positive for cocaine, had his plea rejected by the Cricket Council Appeals' Committee.
After a two and a half hour hearing, Giddins, 25, emerged to tell reporters: "The appeal has been unsuccessful."
His solicitor Michael Lawrence said: "Ed is upset and disappointed by the decision. We felt we had every chance of being successful, although we certainly had a fair hearing.
"We hoped that they would be still able to reduce the sentence. Our grounds were that the original decision was too severe, but the committee did not agree."
The decision means that Giddins, the first English player to be banned for failing a random drugs test, is suspended from all first-class cricket until April 1, 1998.
"Whether this will affect his career in the long run I don't know, but hopefully it won't," Lawrence said.
He added: "Perhaps to say that 10 clubs are interested is exaggerated, but there are clubs who want him to play for them."
In the meantime, Giddins is reported to have set up a shop with Surrey's Nadeem Shahid to sell Christmas trees.
